articles.title: When Michel Siffre emerged from a lightless cave in 1962 after 63 days alone, he was stunned to learn the real date. Cut off from clocks, calendars, and sunlight, he believed it was only August 20 — nearly a month earlier than it really was. His sense of time had compressed so dramatically that two months underground had felt like little more than one.
articles.summary: Michel Siffre, a French speleologist, conducted a pioneering 1962 experiment by spending over two months isolated in the Scarasson cave. Without clocks, calendars, or natural light, his internal sense of time significantly diverged from external reality upon resurfacing. This groundbreaking self-experiment provided crucial insights into human circadian rhythms and the psychological effects of prolonged sensory deprivation, influencing later research in fields like space exploration.

articles.title: First Nations leaders call for more say in allocation of mining claims in Quebec
articles.summary: Indigenous leaders, spearheaded by the Anishinaabe First Nation in Quebec, Canada, are urging the provincial government to modernize its mining claim granting process.
